query_snapshot: For potassium hydroxide solution below 70 percent, which barriers does the archived NIOSH table place in its 8-hour group and which in its 4-hour group?
final_answer:
Evidence-grounded answer:

- The archived NIOSH table entry for "Potassium hydroxide (solution <70% only)" places the following materials in the 8 hr group: Butyl, Natural, Nitrile, PVC, Viton. [NIOSH Recommendations for Chemical Protective Clothing A-Z | NIOSH | CDC: https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/niosh/ncpc/azncpc.html]
- The archived NIOSH table entry for "Potassium hydroxide (solution <70% only)" places the following materials in the 4 hr group: Teflon, PE/EVAL. [NIOSH Recommendations for Chemical Protective Clothing A-Z | NIOSH | CDC: https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/niosh/ncpc/azncpc.html]
- The archived NIOSH table defines the time-group designations as: "8 hr = More than 8 hours of resistance to breakthrough >0.1 g/cm2/min. 4 hr = At least 4 but less than 8 hours of resistance to breakthrough >0.1 g/cm2/min." [NIOSH Recommendations for Chemical Protective Clothing A-Z | NIOSH | CDC: https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/niosh/ncpc/azncpc.html]
